A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EBM review. Their complete text, equations, figures and tables are readable. V2's Appendices A and B largely correspond to historical and stochastic-interpolant material previously in v1's main text.

before.justification: V1 reports original illustrative Monte Carlo results in Section 3.3, Remark 3.1 and Figure 4, estimating KL and Fisher divergences between Gaussian mixtures with 100, 1,000 and 10,000 samples.

after.justification: V2 retains the original Monte Carlo comparison in Section 3.3 and Figure 4, including the three sample sizes and findings about sensitivity to mixture weights.

M1.justification: The review introduces no new proposed algorithm or model. CD and PCD Algorithms 1–2 retain their procedures. V2 expands exposition of existing approaches, including previously cited Jarzynski-based training and sampling-free methods.

E1.justification: The same synthetic Gaussian-mixture illustrations remain. Newly discussed applications, including anomaly detection, molecular modeling and text generation, are literature examples rather than additional tasks evaluated by this work.

E2.justification: The empirical illustration still compares KL and Fisher divergences. Newly reviewed training methods are not evaluated as additional baselines, and removal of the descriptive generation/evaluation table does not remove an experimental comparator.

E3.justification: Figure 4 retains the same Gaussian mixtures, sigmoid-controlled mixture weights, divergence calculations and sample sizes of 100, 1,000 and 10,000. Figure 1's mixture parameters also remain unchanged. No new evaluation protocol is reported.

E4.justification: The sample-size sensitivity analysis of KL versus Fisher divergence in Remark 3.1 and Figure 4 is unchanged. V2's additional limitations and application discussions introduce no new empirical ablation, robustness test or case study.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for the Monte Carlo illustration. The retained sample sizes describe estimator inputs, not repeated experimental runs.

E6.justification: Figures 1 and 4 retain identical plotted content and accompanying findings, including Fisher divergence's weak sensitivity to separated-mode weights at smaller sample sizes. V2 adds no numerical experimental results; experiments mentioned in the expanded training discussion are attributed to other publications.

T1.justification: V2 adds Jarzynski weight recursions and identities for gradients, partition functions and cross-entropy in Equations 102–106, plus explicit denoising-score-matching and NCE objectives in Section 6.2. Lemma 5.1 now specifies normalization and entropy constraints. The stochastic-interpolant proofs in Appendix B are retained material, not new theory.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains an interdisciplinary review connecting EBMs, generative models, sampling and physics. V2 explicitly claims a gap in existing surveys and extends its concluding contribution statement to sampling-free training and proposed research directions involving nonequilibrium methods and physically informed energies.

C2.justification: Sections 3.5–3.6 add substantial discussion of approximation, generation speed, manifold data and when EBMs are practically preferable. Sections 6.1–6.2 expand limitations concerning normalization, sampling bias, noise-distribution choice and derivative costs. Appendix A also adds a stronger interpretation linking normalized probabilities to interpretability.

D1.justification: V2 supplies implementation-oriented details for reviewed approaches: reweighting initialization, learning-rate updates and AdaGrad/ADAM options, plus Gaussian corruption and automatic differentiation for denoising score matching. These are additional documentation, not evidence of changed experiments. No new code release or concrete computational-resource information appears.

R1.justification: V2 explicitly positions the review against surveys by LeCun, Huembeli and Bond-Taylor and substantially expands references on applications, manifold modeling, hybrid models and alternative training. Added works include Gutmann and Hyvärinen on NCE, Gao on flow-contrastive estimation, and Chehab on normalization; this exceeds a bibliographic restyling.

P1.justification: V2 replaces the historical opening with a positioning-focused introduction, revises the history into Appendix A and moves stochastic interpolants to Appendix B. It substantially condenses several model explanations, splits Section 6 into sampling-based and sampling-free methods, and rewrites the conclusion around open perspectives.

P2.justification: V2 adopts TMLR title and running-header styling, changes text width and float placement, and removes v1's Table 2 on generation and evaluation. All six figures retain their graphical content, and Table 1 retains its comparison structure; no new scientific visualization is added.

improvement.justification: V2 improves organization and addresses v1's limited treatment of alternative EBM training and practical applicability. However, the additions introduce mathematical inconsistencies: Section 6.2's denoising objective has a sign inconsistent with its stated energy-score relation and Gaussian corruption, while Equation 106 reverses the cross-entropy arguments relative to Equation 10. Broader coverage therefore comes with reduced reliability in important instructional material, preventing a confident judgment of net overall improvement.
